turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I came in because things have been a bit off lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I just... I haven't really been myself. I’ve been holding it together at work alright, but at home and with my coursework, I’m a lot more wound up and short-tempered than I’m used to being. 

And I’ve started skipping the things that usually keep my head clear. I haven't been going fishing, I dropped my woodworking projects, and I even stopped going to the first-aid workshops I usually like to attend. I just wanted to talk to someone to figure out how to get a handle on it.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient reports emotional and behavioral changes (feeling wound up, short-tempered, and dropping usual activities) that developed in direct response to an identifiable stressor (his father-in-law moving in).

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't really say I feel sad. I'm not down in the dumps or anything like that. It's... well, it's really just the frustration and being wound up, like I mentioned. But no, I don't feel sad.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly states that they do not feel sad or down in the dumps.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different areas of your life, rather than mainly about your father-in-law living with you?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say that. I'm not really a worrier in general. My job is fine, and I'm not stressing over finances or my health or anything like that. It's really just... well, it all comes back to the situation at home with my father-in-law. That's what's got me so wound up, not everything else.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies generalized or excessive worry across multiple areas of life, stating they are not a worrier in general and only react to a specific home situation.

turns.doctor_question: When did you first start feeling this wound up and irritable in relation to your father-in-law moving in?
turns.patient_response: Well, he moved in about four months ago. I'd say I started noticing the strain within the first couple of months. It just kind of built up once the new home routines and the day-to-day caregiving demands really settled in as our new normal. That's when I realized I was getting so on edge.

symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient explicitly confirms feeling 'so on edge' as the caregiving demands and home routines settled in.
symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient reports developing emotional symptoms and strain within the first couple of months in response to an identifiable stressor (father-in-law moving in and caregiving demands).

turns.doctor_question: How much has feeling wound up and irritable interfered with your daily functioning at home or with your coursework?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'm still doing my EMT work just fine, so that hasn't been affected. But... I have fallen behind on some of my paramedic coursework. It's just hard to focus when I'm this tense. And I've also stopped showing up consistently for the community first-aid workshops I usually help out with. I just don't have the patience for it right now.

symptom_reasoning.S059: The patient reports that it is hard to focus when feeling tense, indicating concentration difficulties.
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient states they lack the patience to attend workshops, reflecting exhausted patience and irritability.
